applicability.reason: Performance Lab has critical browser, CLI, persistence, regression and external-runtime workflows whose complete outcomes cannot be established by lower-level tests alone.

target_environments.description: The packaged local Performance Lab browser product: built frontend, installed Python wheel, real loopback API/process and SQLite evidence store.
material_dimensions: packaged Python wheel and built frontend assets

target_environments.description: A real Local LLM Server/model/device path used for runtime, resource, telemetry and deployment-fit claims.
material_dimensions: model artifact revision quantization and effective configuration
load warmup thermal and performance conditions

known_gaps: source checkout rather than packaged product

execution_environments.artifact_surface: published package candidate with installed wheel, built web assets, real loopback API, real SQLite, real Chromium and deterministic external inference fixture
known_gaps: external inference runtime/model is a deterministic fixture
hosted CI hardware is not the representative target device

execution_environments.platform: representative physical device running the external inference runtime
execution_environments.artifact_surface: real Performance Lab run against real Local LLM Server, model and device with retained fingerprint/evidence bundle
known_gaps: a single smoke run does not by itself establish repeated-load variability or thermal envelopes

critical_journeys.claim: User can enter the use-case-first Find best setup journey, understand model + quantization candidate identity and configuration-search/campaign stages, and is not misled into starting an automatic campaign before the campaign engine exists.
residual_gaps: server-owned use-case catalog and benchmark mapping
campaign scheduling and immutable run grouping
critical_journeys.automation_gap_reason: The UX contract and blocked state are executable; automatic campaign execution is not implemented yet.

critical_journeys.claim: User configures a model, reviews a frozen preflight, launches the evaluation, observes progress and can reopen the immutable persisted result.
User can find tested-model evidence with workload and device context without an unsupported opaque winner claim.
User can compare compatible evidence and see only valid quality/runtime/resource trade-off deltas.
An incompatible comparison explains why deltas are invalid and does not render misleading metric deltas.
A failed run exposes an actionable cause and the user can retry successfully without stale run ownership.
Cancelling a run releases owned resources before a subsequent evaluation can start and complete.
Performance Lab retains truthful model/runtime/device identity and runtime/resource evidence when evaluating a real external Local LLM Server on representative hardware.
residual_gaps: real model/runtime identity and effective backend behavior
